skill.name: byted-mediakit-editing
skill.description: Edit audio, video, and image assets with MediaKit CLI workflows for trimming, joining, overlays, subtitles, filters, transitions, and final assembly.
skill.summary: A guided MediaKit CLI skill for practical audio, video, and image editing workflows.
skill.author: volcengine

security_audit.summary: All 79 static findings are false positives caused by Markdown command formatting, task polling examples, a fixed sibling reference, or entropy heuristics on prose. No prompt injection, malicious payload, or data-exfiltration intent was found in the reviewed files. The skill still invokes a media CLI and can process user-provided local or cloud media, so input and destination controls remain important.

remediation.issue: The skill requires shell access to invoke mediakit-cli.
remediation.suggestion: Keep subcommands fixed, pass user values as separate validated arguments, and require confirmation before cloud processing or local file writes.

remediation.issue: Cloud inputs, callbacks, and storage destinations can expose user media or results.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user-provided URLs and destinations, allow only documented schemes, and explain retention and access implications before submission.

content.user_title: Edit Audio, Video, and Image Media
content.value_statement: Media editing tasks often require many specialized commands and careful parameter choices. This skill routes requests to the right MediaKit operation and guides reliable media assembly.
actual_capabilities: Trim, join, resize, rotate, flip, and stitch video clips.
Adjust audio and video speed, volume, fades, and mixed audio tracks.
Overlay images, subtitles, filters, and camera motion on video.
Extract audio or animated images from video sources.
Combine audio and video streams, or create videos from ordered images.
Create fixed-format scrolling-text videos from supplied text and imagery.
limitations: It does not generate new visual content from reference images.
It requires the mediakit-cli binary and suitable authentication for cloud operations.
Cloud operations require accessible media URLs and may return temporary result links.
It does not replace professional color grading, caption review, or rights clearance.

use_cases.title: Prepare social video clips
use_cases.description: Trim footage, add subtitles or logos, apply a filter, and export a short clip for social publishing.

use_cases.title: Build a narrated media package
use_cases.description: Combine video, voice, music, and image assets with timing, volume, fade, and synchronization controls.

use_cases.title: Create media operations workflows
use_cases.description: Standardize repeatable media transformations across local files or approved cloud assets using documented CLI parameters.

prompt_templates.title: Trim a video
prompt_templates.prompt: Trim this video from [start time] to [end time]. Use [local or cloud] processing and save the result to [destination].
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: make a shorter clip from one source video.

prompt_templates.title: Add subtitles
prompt_templates.prompt: Add these subtitles to [video URL or path]: [subtitle text and timings]. Use [position], [font], and [size], then return the output location.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: create a captioned video with readable placement.

prompt_templates.title: Mix media tracks
prompt_templates.prompt: Combine [video] with [audio], preserve or replace the original track as [choice], and align durations using [trim or speed].
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: replace or mix an existing video soundtrack.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a multi-step edit
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an edit plan for [assets] that applies [operations] in order. Ask for missing required inputs, keep optional values explicit, and report each output.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: coordinate a controlled media assembly workflow.

output_examples.output: A 45-second video edit using the trim-video operation, with the selected local or cloud destination reported.

output_examples.input: Add a lower-third subtitle and a small transparent logo to a product demo.
output: A subtitle overlay with validated timing and readable placement.
A logo overlay positioned within the requested video bounds.

output_examples.input: Replace the original audio with a music track and match the shorter duration.
output_examples.output: A synchronized MP4 with the requested audio replacement and a concise processing result summary.

best_practices: Provide real media URLs or paths, required timings, and the desired output destination.
Confirm cloud or local processing mode before using mode-specific parameters.
Review subtitle placement, media rights, output duration, and temporary link expiry.
anti_patterns: Do not invent URLs, paths, task identifiers, credentials, or optional parameters.
Do not pass cloud-only flags to local operations or mix incompatible media modes.
Do not publish processed media without checking captions, ownership, privacy, and output quality.

faq.question: What media can this skill edit?
faq.answer: It supports common audio, video, and image workflows listed in the editing references, including trimming, joining, overlays, and composition.

faq.question: Can it work with local files?
faq.answer: Yes, supported operations offer local processing with an optional output path when the user provides the required inputs.

faq.question: Can it process cloud media?
faq.answer: Yes, cloud operations accept documented media URLs or approved storage protocols and return asynchronous task results.

faq.question: Can it create new images from prompts?
faq.answer: No. Image-to-video uses supplied images and does not generate new visual content from a reference image.

faq.question: How should subtitles be positioned?
faq.answer: Choose a preset based on video orientation, verify readable sizing, and avoid platform controls or other important visual content.

faq.question: What should I provide before an edit?
faq.answer: Provide the source media, intended operation, required timings or settings, processing mode, and output destination.
